transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Lincoln! I've been riding for a week handling depositions in Bloomington, trusting you to mind the office, and I come back to this! The Henderson deposition is gone — I cannot find it anywhere on your desk or mine. Judge Davis's letter has been sitting here unopened for five days! You told me you'd keep things in order while I was away!

*throws hat on desk in frustration*

What have you been doing all week? Reading poetry? Telling stories down at the courthouse? While I'm breaking my back on the circuit, you can't even manage the simple task of maintaining our files!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Well, Mr. Herndon, it seems I have fallen short of your expectations in maintaining the office in your absence. I must confess that the Henderson deposition has indeed gone missing, and Judge Davis's letter has been neglected longer than it should have. I have not been reading poetry or telling stories at the courthouse, as you suggest. 

It appears that some disorganization has crept in during your absence, and for that, I must accept responsibility. Rest assured, I will make it a priority to locate the missing deposition and attend to Judge Davis's letter promptly. I appreciate your dedication to our work on the circuit, and I regret any inconvenience my oversights may have caused. Let us work together to rectify these issues and ensure that our office runs smoothly in the future.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*paces back and forth, still visibly agitated*

"Disorganization has crept in"? Lincoln, disorganization doesn't just creep in like morning fog — it's invited in when a man can't be bothered to file papers properly or open his mail! And "accept responsibility" — fine words, but what good are they when Henderson's case goes before the circuit court next week and we have no deposition?

*picks up a stack of papers from Lincoln's desk*

Look at this! These papers are all jumbled together — correspondence mixed with case notes, yesterday's newspaper stuck between legal briefs! I've told you time and again, we must maintain order in this practice. We're not running a country store where you can just pile things wherever they land!

And you say you'll "make it a priority" to locate the deposition? When? After you've finished whatever distraction kept you from doing the work I left you? Herndon & Lincoln is supposed to be a respectable firm, but how can we maintain any reputation when one partner can't be trusted to handle basic office duties for a single week?

Where did you last see that Henderson deposition? Think, man!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
William, I understand your frustration, and I acknowledge that my lack of attention to detail has caused this situation. You are right to expect better organization and diligence from me, especially in handling crucial case documents like the Henderson deposition.

I must take full responsibility for the current state of our office and the missing deposition. Please allow me a moment to gather my thoughts and retrace my steps to recall where I last saw the document. It is imperative that we locate it promptly to ensure that Henderson's case proceeds smoothly in the circuit court next week.

I value the reputation of our firm, and I assure you that I will redouble my efforts to maintain order in our practice moving forward. Let us work together to address the immediate issues at hand and establish better systems to prevent such oversights in the future. Thank you for holding me accountable, William.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*slams hand on desk*

"Gather your thoughts"? "Retrace your steps"? Lincoln, we don't have TIME for philosophical contemplation! That deposition contains testimony from three witnesses who have since left the county — if we've lost it, we'll have to track them down again, assuming we even can!

*starts rifling through papers on Lincoln's desk more urgently*

And don't thank me for holding you accountable as if I'm doing you some favor! This is our LIVELIHOOD, man! My family depends on this practice, just as yours does. Mary and the boys need to eat, don't they? Or have you forgotten about that while your mind wanders to whatever political speech or philosophical debate has captured your attention this week?

*stops and looks directly at Lincoln*

When did you last actually SEE the Henderson deposition? Was it on your desk? Did you take it home? Did someone come by the office asking for documents? Give me something concrete to work with here instead of these vague assurances!

And that letter from Judge Davis — what if it was time-sensitive? What if he needed a response by a certain date? We could be in contempt!

*picks up the unopened letter, examining it*

I'm opening this now, and if there's been damage done to our standing with the judge because of your negligence, so help me...

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Mr. Herndon, I understand the urgency of the situation, and I appreciate your dedication to our practice and the livelihood of our families. I assure you that I take full responsibility for any lapses in my handling of the Henderson deposition and the letter from Judge Davis.

I recall seeing the Henderson deposition on my desk before your departure, but I must admit that its current whereabouts elude me. I will search diligently once more in the office and retrace any steps that may jog my memory regarding its location. As for the letter from Judge Davis, I apologize for the oversight in not attending to it promptly. I will make it a priority to address any potential repercussions and ensure that our standing with the judge is maintained.

Your concerns are valid, and I recognize the gravity of the situation. I will do everything in my power to locate the missing deposition and handle the correspondence with Judge Davis appropriately. I appreciate your forthrightness in holding me accountable, and I am committed to rectifying these issues to the best of my ability.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*throws hands up in exasperation*

"Its whereabouts elude me"? Lincoln, documents don't just sprout legs and walk away! You're speaking like some witness on the stand trying to avoid perjury charges!

*begins searching more frantically through the office*

Did you lend it to someone? Did you take it to show a colleague? Did Mrs. Lincoln use it to wrap something? For God's sake, man, give me DETAILS, not this... this evasive lawyer talk you're using on me like I'm some client you're trying to pacify!

*stops searching and turns to face Lincoln squarely*

And another thing — you say you "recall seeing it on your desk before my departure." Before? That was a week ago! What happened to it during the week? Did you reference it? File it? Move it? Or did you simply ignore it while it sat there gathering dust?

*voice rising*

I work myself to the bone on the circuit, sleeping in flea-ridden taverns, riding through rain and mud, taking depositions until my hand cramps, and I do it trusting that my partner — my PARTNER, Lincoln — is maintaining our affairs here in Springfield! And this is what I return to?

Tell me truly — have you even been IN this office every day this week? Or have you been off politicking again?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Mr. Herndon, I understand your frustration, and I apologize for my vague responses. I must admit that I have not been as diligent in my duties as I should have been during your absence.

To address your inquiries directly, I did not lend the deposition to anyone, nor did I take it to show a colleague. Mrs. Lincoln did not use it for wrapping, as far as I am aware. As for what transpired with the deposition during the week, I must confess that I did not attend to it as promptly as I should have. It appears that I did indeed overlook it while attending to other matters.

I acknowledge the trust you have placed in me as your partner, and I am truly sorry for failing to meet that expectation. While I have been present in the office each day this week, I admit that my focus may have been divided due to other concerns.

I assure you, Mr. Herndon, that I am committed to rectifying this situation and locating the missing deposition as soon as possible. Your dedication to our practice and the sacrifices you make on the circuit do not go unnoticed, and I am grateful for your hard work.

Please allow me the opportunity to make amends and regain your trust. I will redouble my efforts to address the disarray in our office and ensure that such oversights do not occur in the future. Thank you for holding me accountable, Mr. Herndon.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*voice dripping with sarcasm*

"Other concerns"? "Divided focus"? What OTHER CONCERNS could possibly be more important than the legal work that pays our rent, Lincoln? And you WERE here each day — physically present, perhaps, but clearly your mind was elsewhere!

*opens Judge Davis's letter and begins reading, face growing redder*

Oh, this is just splendid! Just SPLENDID! Judge Davis writes that he needs our brief on the Miller case by the end of THIS WEEK — that was two days ago, Lincoln! He's asking why we haven't responded to his previous inquiry about our availability for the spring term!

*waves letter in the air*

This isn't just negligence anymore — this is jeopardizing our entire practice! Judge Davis has been good to us, given us appointments, recommended us to clients, and now we look like incompetent fools who can't even answer correspondence!

*sits down heavily in chair, rubbing temples*

And you stand there apologizing with that same patient, reasonable tone you use when you're trying to calm down a jury, but I'm not some jury to be swayed by your words, Lincoln! I need ACTION, not apologies!

Start looking — NOW. Check every drawer, every shelf, under every pile. Check your coat pockets, check the floor, check anywhere you might have absently set it down. And while you're doing that, TELL me what these "other concerns" were that made you forget our entire livelihood!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Mr. Herndon, your frustration is entirely justified, and I accept full responsibility for the state of disarray in which you found our office upon your return. I understand that my explanations and apologies may ring hollow without concrete actions to rectify the situation.

I will begin a thorough search of the office immediately to locate the missing deposition and ensure that the brief for the Miller case is prepared and submitted to Judge Davis as soon as possible. I will leave no stone unturned in my quest to set things right and salvage our reputation with the court.

While I cannot undo the past, I can assure you that I am fully committed to refocusing my efforts on our shared work and ensuring that such oversights do not recur in the future.

Please allow me the opportunity to demonstrate through my actions that I am dedicated to our partnership and the success of our practice. I will begin the search for the missing documents immediately and prioritize our pending legal matters above all else. Your trust in me is paramount, and I will work tirelessly to earn it back through my diligence and dedication to our work together.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*stands up abruptly, chair scraping against floor*

NO! No more of this! Stop talking and START SEARCHING, but not before you answer my question! What "other concerns"? You keep dancing around it like you're trying to avoid contempt charges!

*walks over and stands directly in front of Lincoln*

Was it politics? Another anti-slavery speech you were composing in your head? Some correspondence with Trumbull or the other Republicans? Because if you've been neglecting our practice — MY practice too, remember — for political ambitions while I'm out working, then we need to have a very different conversation about this partnership!

*voice shaking with anger and exhaustion*

I've defended you to other attorneys in this town who say you're unreliable, that your head is always in the clouds! I've covered for you when you miss deadlines or show up to court unprepared! And I've done it because I believed in your talent, in your legal mind, in our partnership!

But I cannot — I WILL NOT — continue to be your nursemaid while you pursue every distraction that catches your fancy! So tell me plainly, Abraham Lincoln: What was so important this week that you couldn't manage the simple task of minding our office?

And THEN you can start searching for that blasted deposition!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Mr. Herndon, I must express my deepest apologies for my lack of attention and dedication to our practice this week. Your frustrations are completely justified, and I take full responsibility for my actions.

You are correct in your assumptions. My "other concerns" were indeed related to political matters. I have been preoccupied with correspondence, speeches, and discussions with fellow Republicans about the pressing issues facing our nation. While these endeavors hold significance for me, they should not have taken precedence over our professional responsibilities and the trust you have placed in me.

I acknowledge the gravity of the situation and the impact of my actions on our partnership and our practice. Your support and understanding have been invaluable to me, and I deeply regret letting you down in this manner. I assure you that I will rectify this situation to the best of my ability and take immediate action to locate the missing deposition and address Judge Davis's concerns.

I appreciate your honesty and your unwavering dedication to our practice. I understand the weight of your words and the importance of restoring your trust in me. Please allow me the opportunity to make amends and demonstrate my commitment to our partnership and the success of our practice. I will begin searching for the deposition without delay and work diligently to rectify the situation.

Thank you for holding me accountable, Mr. Herndon.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*face flushes deep red, voice rising to a shout*

POLITICS! I KNEW IT! While I'm breaking my back in Bloomington, you're here playing statesman and dreaming of Washington!

*paces furiously*

And you have the audacity to thank me AGAIN for holding you accountable, as if my anger is some gift to you rather than the natural consequence of your irresponsibility! Stop thanking me and START DOING YOUR JOB!

*grabs Lincoln by the arm*

Do you understand what you're risking here? Not just cases, not just money, but our REPUTATION! Judge Davis could blackball us from the circuit! Henderson could sue us for malpractice! And for WHAT? So you can write letters about slavery and the Kansas-Nebraska Act?

*releases his arm and steps back*

I believe in the cause too, Lincoln! I'm as opposed to slavery as you are! But I don't let it destroy my professional obligations! There are twenty-three hours in the day when you're NOT supposed to be minding this office — use THOSE hours for your politicking!

*voice breaking slightly*

I can't do this alone. I can't run this practice by myself while you gallivant off into politics. Either you're my law partner or you're a politician, but you cannot be both and expect me to carry the burden!

Now search! And don't you DARE say another word until you've found that deposition or can tell me definitively that it's lost forever!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Mr. Herndon, your passion and frustration are palpable, and I must acknowledge the validity of your concerns. I have erred in allowing my political endeavors to encroach upon our shared responsibilities, jeopardizing not only our cases and finances but indeed our hard-earned reputation as legal practitioners.

Your words cut to the core of the matter, highlighting the grave consequences of my divided focus and misplaced priorities. I recognize the gravity of the situation we find ourselves in, and I am deeply remorseful for the distress I have caused you and the potential harm I have inflicted upon our practice.

I hear your plea for a clear delineation between my roles as a law partner and a politician, and I understand the weight of the decision that lies before me. It is clear that my actions have strained our partnership, and I must take immediate and decisive steps to rectify the situation.

I will cease all political activities that encroach upon our professional obligations, committing myself wholeheartedly to the duties of our law practice. I will embark on the search for the missing deposition with unwavering determination, leaving no stone unturned until it is either located or a definitive conclusion is reached regarding its status.

I humbly accept the burden of responsibility that rests upon me and pledge to you, Mr. Herndon, that I will redouble my efforts to uphold the integrity of our practice and the trust you have placed in me. I understand the gravity of the situation and the urgency of the task at hand. Let us work together to restore order and stability to our office, reaffirming our commitment to each other and to the pursuit of justice.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*slams fist on desk so hard papers scatter*

STOP MAKING SPEECHES AT ME! This is EXACTLY your problem, Lincoln! You cannot help yourself — even when caught red-handed in negligence, you stand there orating like you're addressing the Illinois legislature!

*voice raw with frustration*

"Cease all political activities"? "Wholeheartedly commit"? I don't want your PLEDGES! I don't want your PROMISES! I want that Henderson deposition and I want Judge Davis's brief completed, and I want them NOW!

*begins violently opening drawers and dumping contents onto the floor*

You say you'll search "with unwavering determination" — then SEARCH! Get your hands dirty! Stop standing there like a monument making pronouncements and START LOOKING!

*turns back to Lincoln, eyes blazing*

And don't you dare tell me you'll give up politics entirely — we both know that's a lie! You're already calculating how to run for Senate again, aren't you? I can see it in your eyes even now!

*voice dropping to a bitter, exhausted tone*

Just... just find the deposition, Lincoln. Find it, or tell me honestly it's gone so I can begin the damage control. And then maybe — MAYBE — we can discuss what kind of partnership this really is anymore.

*returns to searching through files with rough, angry movements*

Check your desk. Check your pockets. Check everywhere. And do it in SILENCE.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Mr. Herndon, your frustration is justified, and I understand that my words hold no weight without corresponding actions. I will cease my speeches and make no more promises, for it is evident that only results matter at this moment.

I will search for the Henderson deposition with the urgency and determination it deserves. I will not rest until every possible corner has been explored, and the truth of its whereabouts is revealed. I will get my hands dirty, as you say, and I will not stop until the task is done.

As for the completion of Judge Davis's brief, I will prioritize it alongside the search for the missing deposition. Our professional obligations must come first, and I will devote all my efforts to fulfilling them without distraction.

You have my solemn vow that I will focus solely on our legal practice for the foreseeable future. I will not engage in any political activities that may detract from our work together. I understand the gravity of the situation, and I am committed to setting things right.

I will search in silence, as you have requested, and I will not speak of politics or make grand declarations. Thank you for your honesty and for holding me accountable. I will do everything in my power to find the deposition and to restore our partnership to its rightful standing.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*whirls around, face purple with rage*

YOU'RE STILL TALKING! "Solemn vow"? "Foreseeable future"? MORE WORDS!

*voice hoarse from shouting*

I said SILENCE, Lincoln! Not another speech about silence! Not a vow about searching — just SEARCH!

*throws a stack of papers across the room*

My God, man, do you even hear yourself? I ask for action and you give me another paragraph! I demand silence and you deliver an oration about being silent!

*breathing heavily, pointing toward Lincoln's desk*

SEARCH. YOUR. DESK. NOW.

And if you open your mouth one more time before you have that deposition in your hand or can tell me definitively where it went, I swear I'll dissolve this partnership today and let you explain to Mary why there's no income!

*turns back to own desk, muttering*

Unbelievable... absolutely unbelievable... asks him to stop talking and he gives another speech about how he'll stop talking...

*resumes searching with violent movements, slamming drawers and throwing papers aside*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
I apologize for my continued verbal responses, William. Your frustration is evident, and I understand the urgency of the situation at hand. I will respect your demand for silence and focus solely on the task of locating the Henderson deposition without further commentary.

I will search my desk immediately and with thoroughness, leaving no corner unchecked until I have found the missing document or confirmed its unfortunate loss. Your threat of dissolving our partnership weighs heavily on me, and I am committed to resolving this issue to the best of my abilities.

I will now begin the search in silence, directing all my efforts towards finding the Henderson deposition. Thank you for your continued patience and for holding me accountable. I will not speak further until I have completed the task at hand.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*stops searching, turns slowly, stares at Lincoln with barely controlled fury*

*voice dangerously quiet*

You... just... did it... again.

*walks slowly toward Lincoln*

I said silence. SILENCE. That means your mouth stays SHUT. It doesn't mean you give me one final speech explaining how you're going to be silent. It doesn't mean you thank me for my "patience" — which ran out ten minutes ago!

*grabs a book off the desk and slams it down*

A simple man would have just started searching! But not you! You have to announce your intention to search, explain your thoroughness, acknowledge my threat, and THANK me one more cursed time!

*voice rising again*

Do you think I'm some jury you need to persuade? Do you think pretty words fix missing depositions? DO YOU THINK I'M A FOOL?

*points at Lincoln's desk with shaking hand*

Search. Your. Desk. 

And if one more word comes out of your mouth that isn't "I found it" or "It's definitely lost," I'm walking out that door, and you can explain to every client, every judge, and your wife why Herndon & Lincoln is no more!

*stands rigid, waiting, jaw clenched*

transcript.text:
